PROJECT STORY / 01 · DETAILED CASE STUDY
SMART
WASTE.
01 / PROBLEM

Waste gets mixed.

Organic, recyclable, dry and special waste can require different handling. When everything enters the same stream, sorting becomes harder and useful material can be lost.

02 / OBJECTIVE

Make sorting understandable.

The prototype explores an automated classification workflow: detect an item, decide its category and communicate the correct destination.

03 / HOW IT WORKS

Input → Processing → Decision → Output

OBJECT / SENSOR INPUT→MICROCONTROLLER→CLASSIFICATION LOGIC→LED / SERVO / DISPLAY→CORRECT BIN
04 / HARDWARE

Prototype components

Possible implementation: Arduino-class controller, object/weight/proximity sensing, indicator LEDs, buzzer and servo-based sorting mechanism.

05 / SOFTWARE

Control logic

Read the sensor → validate the reading → map the reading to a category → activate the output → reset for the next item.

06 / SOCIETAL USE

Why it can matter

A clear feedback mechanism can make correct disposal easier to understand at campuses, public spaces and community facilities. A production system would require testing, safety review and reliable classification before deployment.

07 / FUTURE

Computer vision

Camera-based recognition and machine learning could expand the range of objects the system can classify.

08 / FUTURE

Connected analytics

Bin fill-level monitoring and usage data could support collection planning and maintenance.

PROJECT STORY / 02 · DETAILED CASE STUDY
SMART
PARKING.
01 / PROBLEM

Searching wastes time.

In a busy parking area, drivers may not know which spaces are occupied until they reach them.

02 / OBJECTIVE

Show availability early.

Detect each space and turn raw occupancy signals into a simple availability view.

03 / HOW IT WORKS

Detect → Count → Display

SLOT SENSOR→MICROCONTROLLER→OCCUPANCY STATE→LED / DISPLAY→DRIVER
04 / HARDWARE

Prototype components

Distance/proximity sensors, controller board, LEDs or display and power circuitry form the basic prototype.

05 / LOGIC

Space state

Each sensor is read continuously. A threshold determines occupied/free state, then the total availability is updated.

06 / SOCIETAL USE

Why it can matter

Parking guidance can reduce unnecessary searching and make space usage easier to understand. A real deployment would need accurate sensing, environmental testing and reliable failure handling.

07 / FUTURE

Mobile dashboard

Live availability could be shown on a web or mobile interface.

08 / FUTURE

Smart-city layer

Analytics could help operators understand peak periods, occupancy and maintenance needs.
